title: Compatible K-flat representatives of a semilinear coefficient tower
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $O$, and a scheme $T$. Put $R=\mathcal O_{E,T}$ and $B_n=(O/\ell^n)_T$ for $n\geq1$, and let $\operatorname{Tow}(T,O)$ be the abelian category of semilinear coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Let $C_\bullet\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(T,O))$, with exact derived evaluations $C_n\in D(B_n)$ and transitions $t_n:C_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{B_{n+1}\to B_n}C_n$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. There exist complexes $Q_n$ of $B_n$-modules, K-flat with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex], semilinear chain maps $q_n:Q_{n+1}\to Q_n$, and isomorphisms $e_n:Q_n\xrightarrow{\sim}C_n$ in $D(B_n)$ such that $\operatorname{Res}(e_n)\circ Q(q_n)=t_n\circ e_{n+1}$ in $D(B_{n+1})$; here $Q$ denotes localization and the restriction is along $B_{n+1}\to B_n$. The longer chain transitions are composites and represent all the original composite transitions.

After restricting scalars to $R$, this compatible family lifts to an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(R)))$ between the strict $R$-tower $Q_\bullet$ and the levelwise restriction of $C_\bullet$. Its evaluations are the specified $e_n$; applying total derived inverse limit respects every evaluation projection [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Only existence of such a lift is asserted. For every $1\leq m\leq n$, the chain map $Q_n\otimes_{B_n}B_m\to Q_m$, $x\otimes b\mapsto bq_{n,m}(x)$, represents, via the $e_n$ and K-flat change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], the original canonical reduction map $C_n\otimes^L_{B_n}B_m\to C_m$ in $D(B_m)$.

proof.text: Put $X=\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{proét}})$ and $I=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$. By det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian, $\operatorname{Tow}(T,O)=\operatorname{Mod}_{X^I}(B_\bullet)$. Use the small site $\mathbf N_{\geq1}\times T_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with the vertical topology of lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-topology. A presheaf on it is an inverse sequence of presheaves on the original site. Its sheaf condition says exactly that each vertical slice $F(n,-)$ is a sheaf. Indeed, let every slice be a sheaf, let $S$ cover $(n,U)$, so its slice $S_n=\{g:(1_n,g)\in S\}$ covers $U$, and let $x$ be a matching family on $S$. Glue $x$ on $S_n$ to $s\in F(n,U)$. For $(a,f)\in S$ with $a:n'\to n$, the sieve $S_a=\{g:(a,g)\in S\}$ on $U$ contains $S_n$, because $(a,g)=(1_n,g)\circ(a,1)$; the family $(x_{(a,g)})_{g\in S_a}$ matches in the sheaf $F(n',-)$, and $F(a,1)s$ restricts to it on the covering $S_n$, since $x_{(a,g)}=F(a,1)x_{(1_n,g)}$ there. By separatedness $F(a,1)s$ is its gluing, so $s$ restricts to $x_{(a,f)}$; uniqueness holds already on $S_n$. Conversely, for a cover $R$ of $U$, the sieve generated by the arrows $(1_n,g)$, $g\in R$, has slice $R$, hence covers $(n,U)$; a matching family on $R$ extends to it by horizontal restrictions, so gluing on $(n,U)$ gives gluing in $F(n,-)$. Hence the sheaves on this site are the inverse sequences in $X$, with the same morphisms, namely $X^I$. The presheaf $(n,U)\mapsto B_n(U)$, with horizontal restrictions given by coefficient reduction, is consequently a sheaf of commutative rings. Its module sheaves are precisely the stated semilinear towers: the restriction on modules along $n\to n+1$ in the site is $B_{n+1}$-linear after restriction along $B_{n+1}\to B_n$. This identifies the ringed-site module category with the given tower category, without assuming constant coefficients in the index variable.

source.place: Definition 3.5.3, printed p.24; explicit vertical-site realization using the cited diagram-topology node

proof.text: For each $n$, evaluation $v_n:X^I\to X$ is the inverse image of a geometric morphism $i_n:X\to X^I$. Explicitly its right adjoint on sheaves of sets sends $F$ to the tower with value $F$ at $j\geq n$ and the terminal sheaf at $j<n$, with identity maps above $n$ and the unique remaining maps. A map from a tower $A_\bullet$ to this tower is uniquely determined by $A_n\to F$: at $j\geq n$ it is its composite with $A_j\to A_n$. This proves the adjunction. Evaluation preserves finite limits because limits of towers are componentwise. Since $i_n^{-1}B_\bullet=B_n$, use the identity structural ring map; the module pullback $i_n^*$ is exactly evaluation, by the tensor unitor $M_n\otimes_{B_n}B_n\cong M_n$.

source.place: Definition 3.5.3; explicit evaluation adjunction on the inverse-system topos

proof.text: Represent $C_\bullet$ by a cochain complex $M$ in the tower category, together with an isomorphism $a:Q(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_\bullet$. Apply lem-pc-kflat-resolution to the ringed site of step 1. It gives a quasi-isomorphism $p:P\to M$ which is a morphism of complexes of semilinear towers, with $P$ K-flat over $B_\bullet$ and all terms flat over $B_\bullet$. In particular its component maps and horizontal transitions already commute as chain maps. No separate lifting of morphisms between individually chosen resolutions is required.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution, applied on the vertical diagram site

proof.text: Apply lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback to each $i_n$ of step 2 and to $P$. Its hypotheses are precisely K-flatness and flatness of every term, both furnished by step 3. Thus $Q_n=i_n^*P=P_n$ is K-flat over $B_n$ and has flat $B_n$-module terms. The map $p_n:P_n\to M_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism because evaluation is exact by det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian. Notice that this argument makes no flatness assertion about $B_{n+1}\to B_n$, or about restriction to $R$.

source.place: Tag 0G7E, lemma-pullback-K-flat; exact evaluation supplied by the coefficient-tower lemma

proof.text: Let $q_n:P_{n+1}\to P_n$ be the horizontal chain transition and put $e_n=a_n\circ Q(p_n)$. The chain square is $\operatorname{Res}(p_n)q_n=t_n^M p_{n+1}$. Localizing it and then using the naturality square for evaluation of the tower isomorphism $a$ yields $\operatorname{Res}(e_n)Q(q_n)=t_ne_{n+1}$. For $m<n$, set $q_{n,m}=q_m\cdots q_{n-1}$, and $q_{n,n}=1$. Substituting the adjacent square successively cancels the intervening $e_j$ and proves the same square for every composite transition. The chain composites are semilinear for the composite coefficient quotient by the defining scalar equation.

source.place: Preliminary coherent-tower realization before the coefficient-fiber calculation; explicit chain squares

proof.text: The functor $U:\operatorname{Tow}(T,O)\to\operatorname{Fun}(I,\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ restricts scalars through the compatible projections $R\to B_n$ at every level and keeps each underlying sheaf and transition. It is exact: its component restriction functors keep kernels and cokernels of underlying abelian sheaves, and exactness of both tower categories is componentwise. Hence it sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms and induces $D(U)$. The isomorphism $D(U)(a\circ Q(p))$ is the required lift; its evaluations are exactly $\operatorname{Res}_{R\to B_n}(e_n)$ since all functors were induced on the same complex and chain map. Apply the total derived inverse-limit functor of lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit to this very isomorphism. Define the evaluation projections by the first arrow of its natural product triangle followed by the n-th product projection. Naturality of that triangle gives $\pi_n^{U(C)}\circ R\lim(D(U)(aQ(p)))=\operatorname{Res}(e_n)\circ\pi_n^{U(P)}$. This constructs the asserted lift and its projection compatibility.

source.place: Tag 0940, section-derived-limits, and Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, on the constant R tower site

proof.text: Fix $1\leq m\leq n$. Ordinary scalar extension is left adjoint to restriction by lem-pur-system-scalar-model. The adjunct of $q_{n,m}:P_n\to\operatorname{Res}P_m$ is the chain map $\beta_{n,m}:P_n\otimes_{B_n}B_m\to P_m$ given locally by $x\otimes b\mapsto bq_{n,m}(x)$. This is balanced because $q_{n,m}(cx)=\bar c q_{n,m}(x)$; it commutes with the differential because $q_{n,m}$ does. The normalized transpose formula in the cited scalar-model statement and the K-flat computation of lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings identify $Q(\beta_{n,m})$ with the derived adjunct of $Q(q_{n,m})$. By clause (3) of det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian the reduction map is the one induced by the transitions, that is, the derived scalar-extension adjunct of the transition $C_n\to\operatorname{Res}C_m$; for the tower $Q(P)$ this transition is $Q(q_{n,m})$, so $\mathrm{red}_{n,m}(Q(P))=Q(\beta_{n,m})$ under the K-flat isomorphism $P_n\otimes^L_{B_n}B_m\cong P_n\otimes_{B_n}B_m$. Naturality of the reduction maps from det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian, applied to the tower isomorphism $aQ(p)$, therefore gives $e_m Q(\beta_{n,m})=\mathrm{red}_{n,m}(C)\circ(e_n\otimes^L_{B_n}B_m)$ under that computation. This is the original canonical reduction map, including $m=n$, where $\beta$ is the tensor unitor.

lean.note: The predicate packages precisely the model conclusions, using the recorded tower category, flat-term K-flat predicate, normalized reductions and actual completed coefficient projections. One complex of towers supplies all coherent chain transitions. No boundedness, tower normalization, quotient flatness or universe equality is assumed. The normalized scalar data and pure tensors use def-weil-pbc-system-scalar-model; derived localizations use HasDerivedCategory.standard from def-weil-abstract-derived-category, not the scalar-model existence theorem.
